title: SIB-1 sensor-interface board in KiCad
card_detail: Four-stage schematic, custom library, 2-layer PCB, DRC clean.
context: A small sensor-interface board for an ATmega328P: protected 5 V input and 3.3 V LDO, an NTC front end with an anti-alias filter, an I2C temperature sensor and a calibration EEPROM. The circuit is split into four functional stages, each on its own schematic sheet, and every symbol and footprint comes from a library built for the board. Python scripts drive KiCad 7 to generate the design from one description and check it. The board has not been fabricated or bench-tested.

statement.tool: KiCad 7 schematic, PCB and DRC, scripted with Python
statement.built: 15 symbols, 14 footprints, 5 schematic sheets and a 36-part 2-layer board with BOM and Gerbers
statement.result: KiCad's netlist matches the design net by net; DRC reports 0 errors and 0 unconnected pads

flow_label: Library to schematic to PCB to checks
method_note: Each stage is its own sheet, so the analog front end can be reused on another board as one block. KiCad 7 has no command-line ERC, so the exported netlist is compared with the design and checked against ERC-style rules. Two tests confirm the checker catches a broken connection and a missing power flag.

spec: 54 x 42 mm, 2 layers, 0.2 mm clearance, 0.6/0.3 mm vias
Power, MCU, NTC front end, I2C sensor and EEPROM
36 placed parts, 25 BOM lines, 22 nets, 15 no-connect pins
results: Gerber and drill files, BOM, schematic PDF
decisions: Ratiometric NTC divider on AVCC with a 1 % divider resistor, taken from the SPICE Monte Carlo.
One decoupling capacitor for each MCU supply pin, plus AVCC and AREF.
VIN/3 on ADC1 so firmware can flag a low input before readings drift.
EEPROM write protect tied low and fixed I2C addresses (0x48, 0x50) for the bring-up firmware.
verification: 13 tests check pin and pad numbers for every part, KiCad's netlist against the design, the ERC-style rules, DRC and that every part sits inside the board outline.
